# NNN-GHL-manager

> Multi-sub-account management dashboard for a marketing agency running on GoHighLevel (GHL).
> Stack: Svelte 5 SPA (`frontend/`) + Go stdlib backend proxy (`backend/`) + Rust workers (`workers/`).
> One inviolable rule: GHL tokens (`pit-…`) live **server-side only** and never reach the browser.

This file orients an AI coding agent (Codex / Claude) — and any human contributor — working in this
repo. **Read it first, then the docs it links.** Everything below is grounded in the actual code as of
the latest commit on `main`. If this file ever disagrees with the code, the code wins — fix this file.

**You work on `dev/Miriam` and on `feature/*` branches you cut from it — never on `main`.** As a full
contributor you may change any file — frontend, backend, workers, or docs — **except** you must never
violate a "Hard rule" below, and you must follow the **Branching & workflow** and **Documentation
discipline** sections exactly. They are not optional.

---

## Hard rules (never break — this is the security contract)

1. **Tokens are server-side only (ADR-001).** A GHL `pit-…` token must NEVER be sent to the browser,
   written to a file, logged, or returned in an API response. The browser calls `/api/*`; the Go
   backend injects the token. Responses may carry `hasToken: bool` — never the token value.
   Enforced in `backend/internal/proxy/client.go`, `backend/internal/store/vault.go`,
   `backend/internal/handlers/*`. Any new endpoint must keep this invariant.
2. **Keep the SSRF guard on.** Outbound calls are host-locked to the GHL API base; the live-page funnel
   audit only fetches validated public hosts. Don't remove the host/IP checks (`guardPublicHost` /
   `isPublicIP` in `handlers/funnels.go`).
3. **Backend stays standard-library-only.** No web framework, no new Go dependency without discussion —
   `backend/go.mod` has zero `require`s; keep it that way.
4. **Never commit secrets.** No `pit-…` tokens, no `.env`, no `*.key` / `*.cer` in commits. Tokens are
   entered at runtime in the Connect page, never hardcoded.
5. **Respect the GHL API ceiling** (see below). Don't promise a write feature GHL's API can't do.
6. **Never touch `main`.** Do not commit, merge, rebase, push, or open a PR into `main`. All your work
   lives on `dev/Miriam` and on `feature/*` branches cut from it. Promoting `dev/Miriam` → `main` is the
   lead dev's job — not a step you ever run. (See **Branching & workflow**.)
7. **Docs ship with the code that changed them.** Read a module's docs before you touch it; update those
   docs in the *same* feature branch when behavior changes. A change with stale docs is **not done**.
   (See **Documentation discipline**.)

---

## Run & verify

```bash
# backend API → http://localhost:8091   (port is hardcoded; 8080/8090/9090 are taken by Docker on the lead dev's box)
cd backend && go run ./cmd/server

# frontend SPA → http://localhost:5173   (proxies /api → :8091)
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev
```

Before every commit, both must pass:

```bash
cd backend  && go build ./... && go vet ./...
cd frontend && npm run check        # svelte-check — must report 0 errors
```

No database, no env vars, no secrets are needed to run it. The token vault is **in-memory and cleared
on backend restart** — reconnect accounts via the Connect page after each restart.

---

## Current state — frontend pages (`frontend/src/routes/`)

Nav lives in `+layout.svelte`. Each page is a `…/+page.svelte` that calls the backend through
`src/lib/api/client.ts` (`apiGet` / `apiPost` / `apiDelete`).

| Route | File | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | `+page.svelte` | Home / landing | ✅ |
| `/connect` | `connect/+page.svelte` | Paste an agency or location `pit-…`; validates + stores server-side; resolves the friendly account name from the `Location Name` custom value | ✅ |
| `/accounts` | `accounts/+page.svelte` | Account library (token presence, domain/meta), CSV import/export, select-to-scope | ✅ |
| `/custom-values` | `custom-values/+page.svelte` | Bulk view/edit custom values across accounts, brand presets, New-Patient-Link (NPL) scanner, delete a CV | ✅ |
| `/schema` | `schema/+page.svelte` | Per-account objects + custom-field schema viewer | ✅ |
| `/automations` | `automations/+page.svelte` | Read-only workflow list (GHL Workflows API is list-only) | ✅ |
| `/dashboard` | `dashboard/+page.svelte` | Leads-by-day, top sources, per-account analytics | ✅ |
| `/funnels` | `funnels/+page.svelte` | Funnel list + live-page pixel/UTM audit + duplicate-pixel detection + assisted-manual fix + per-funnel **Verify** | ◐ |
| `/dialers` | `dialers/+page.svelte` | Phone-number spam reputation (research-complete; not wired to a vendor yet) | 📝 |
| `/help` | `help/+page.svelte` | Renders `docs/MANUAL.md` in-app via `lib/utils/markdown.ts` | ✅ |

State stores: `src/lib/stores/*.svelte.ts` (Svelte 5 runes — `accounts`, `dialers`, `session`,
`extension-bridge`). Shared data: `src/lib/data/` (`brand-presets.ts`, `pixel-snippets.ts`).

## Current state — backend API (authoritative source: `backend/cmd/server/main.go`)

Go 1.23, `net/http.ServeMux` (method+pattern routing). Middleware chain: CORS → RateLimit → Auth
(Auth is a **no-op stub** until the Auth milestone).

```
POST   /api/connect                          agency PIT → list sub-accounts
POST   /api/connect/location                 location-scoped PIT → single sub-account
POST   /api/tokens/{locationId}              save / replace a location token
GET    /api/accounts                         connected accounts
GET    /api/accounts/library                 saved account library (+ CSV)
PUT    /api/accounts/{locationId}/meta       update account metadata (name / domain)
GET    /api/cv                               list custom values (scope with ?locationIds=)
GET    /api/cv/npl-scan                      New-Patient-Link booking-link audit
POST   /api/cv/bulk                          bulk update custom values  ← the ONLY GHL write
GET    /api/cv/{locationId}/{cvId}           single custom value
DELETE /api/cv/{locationId}/{cvId}           delete a custom value
GET    /api/customfields/{locationId}        custom-field schema   (GHL Version 2021-04-15)
GET    /api/objects/{locationId}             object schema         (GHL Version 2023-02-21)
GET    /api/workflows/{locationId}           list workflows (read-only)
GET    /api/funnels/{locationId}             list funnels
GET    /api/funnels/{locationId}/audit       live-page pixel/UTM audit (?funnelId= ?fresh=1)
PUT    /api/funnels/page/{pageId}            funnel page update — see GHL ceiling (assisted-manual)
GET    /api/dashboard/{locationId}/contacts  dashboard analytics
POST   /api/numbers/library                  dialer numbers library
/api/ghl/*                                   generic GHL proxy (server-side token injection)
```

Handlers: `backend/internal/handlers/*.go`. Proxy + Version logic: `backend/internal/proxy/client.go`
and `backend/internal/store/version.go`.

## Architecture

- **frontend/** — SvelteKit + Svelte 5 runes SPA. Calls `/api/*` only; never sees a token.
- **backend/** — Go stdlib HTTP server on :8091. `cmd/server/main.go` (entry) → `internal/handlers`
  (per-module) → `internal/proxy` (host-locked GHL client) → `internal/store` (in-memory token vault +
  metadata). `internal/middleware` = CORS, rate-limit, auth-stub.
- **workers/** — Rust (`number-matcher`, `csv-processor`). Standalone; not yet wired into the backend.
- **GHL Version header is per-endpoint** — resolved in `store.GHLVersionFor(path)`:
  objects → `2023-02-21`, customValues / customFields → `2021-04-15`, everything else → `2021-07-28`.
  The wrong version makes GHL reject the call. Don't hardcode a version inside a handler.

## The GHL API ceiling (read before promising a feature)

GHL's public API v2 is **read-rich, write-poor**:

- ✅ You can READ almost everything.
- ✅ The only meaningful WRITE is custom values (`POST /api/cv/bulk` → GHL `PUT customValues`).
- ⛔ There is **no** funnel/page write endpoint for any auth type. Funnel pixel fixes are
  **assisted-manual**: audit the live page → show the exact snippet + a deep link → operator pastes &
  publishes → Verify re-checks.
- ⛔ Workflows are list-only.

Full detail: `docs/module-capabilities-and-limits.md` and `docs/ghl-api-surface.md`.

## Gotchas (these will bite you)

- **GHL returns some numbers as floats.** A custom-field `position` comes back as e.g. `281.25`. Decode
  such fields as `float64`, not `int` (an `int` decode caused a 502 — see `handlers/customfields.go`).
- **Per-account PIT.** Each connected account uses its own `pit-…`; there is no single global token.
- **In-memory vault.** A backend restart drops all connected tokens — reconnect via `/connect`.
- **Svelte 5 runes**, not legacy stores: state is `$state`, derived is `$derived`. Match the existing
  `*.svelte.ts` files rather than introducing a different pattern.

## What you can change (full-contributor scope on `dev/Miriam`)

Everything in the repo is fair game — frontend pages, backend handlers, Rust workers, and docs —
**subject to the Hard rules above.** Practical guidance:

- Documentation lives in `docs/` (+ root `README.md` + this file). Keep `docs/MANUAL.md` in sync when
  you change a feature — it's what `/help` renders for users.
- When you change a backend endpoint, update the API list in this file **and** in `docs/MANUAL.md` §5.
- When you add a page, add it to `+layout.svelte` nav **and** to the page table above.

## Documentation map (respect these — they encode hard-won decisions)

- `docs/MANUAL.md` — full feature + API reference (also served at `/help`). **Start here.**
- `docs/module-capabilities-and-limits.md` — exactly what GHL's API can and cannot do.
- `docs/ghl-api-surface.md`, `docs/ghl-api-v2-auth-model.md` — GHL endpoints + auth / version model.
- `docs/security-audit.md` — the token / SSRF security posture (the Hard rules, formalized).
- `docs/module-specs/01-…-10-….md` — per-module specs (what each module should do).
- `docs/funnels/*` — funnels API contract + verified implementation path.
- `docs/architecture/platform-architecture-and-migration.md` — the longer-term CRM + CMS direction.
- `README.md` — public overview, milestones, roadmap.

## Branching & workflow (follow exactly)

```
main                      ← PROTECTED. Never commit / merge / rebase / push / PR here. Lead dev only.
 └─ dev/Miriam            ← your integration branch. Features land here, and ONLY here.
     ├─ feature/<slug>    ← one branch per feature or fix. Cut from dev/Miriam, merge back to it.
     └─ fix/<slug>
```

**Never work directly on `dev/Miriam` for a feature, and never work on `main` at all.** Every new
feature or fix gets its own short-lived branch off `dev/Miriam`.

### 1. Start a feature — branch off `dev/Miriam`
```bash
git switch dev/Miriam
git pull origin dev/Miriam            # start from the latest
git switch -c feature/<slug>          # e.g. feature/dashboard-date-filter  (use fix/<slug> for bugfixes)
```

### 2. Build it
- **Read the docs first** (see **Documentation discipline**).
- Make small, focused commits. Keep code **and the docs it affects in the same commit**.
- Run the verify gate before every commit:
  ```bash
  cd backend  && go build ./... && go vet ./...
  cd frontend && npm run check        # must report 0 errors
  ```

### 3. Finish — merge the feature branch into `dev/Miriam` (never `main`)
```bash
# from a clean feature branch (verify passes + docs updated):
git switch dev/Miriam
git pull origin dev/Miriam            # in case it moved
git merge --no-ff feature/<slug>      # --no-ff keeps the feature as one reviewable bubble
git push origin dev/Miriam
git branch -d feature/<slug>          # optional: delete the merged branch
```
If you want a review first, push the feature branch and open a PR **into `dev/Miriam`** — never into `main`.

### Never (hard "no")
- ❌ `git switch main` to work, `git commit` on `main`, `git merge` into `main`, `git push origin main`, or any PR targeting `main`.
- ❌ Committing a feature straight onto `dev/Miriam` (cut a `feature/*` branch instead).
- ❌ Merging a branch that hasn't passed the verify gate or whose docs are stale.

Getting `dev/Miriam` onto `main` is the **lead dev's** review step — not yours.

## Documentation discipline (verify before, update after)

Docs are part of the change, not an afterthought. Two non-negotiable halves:

**Before you change anything — verify the docs:**
1. Read `llms.txt` (this file) + `docs/MANUAL.md`.
2. Read the module's spec: `docs/module-specs/NN-<module>.md`.
3. Anything touching GHL behavior → read `docs/module-capabilities-and-limits.md` +
   `docs/ghl-api-surface.md` so you don't build something GHL's API can't do.

If the code already disagrees with a doc, that's a bug — reconcile it (fix the doc or the code) and say so.

**After you change anything — update the docs in the same feature branch:**

| You changed… | Update… |
|---|---|
| A feature's behavior | `docs/MANUAL.md` (it's what `/help` renders) |
| A backend endpoint (added / removed / changed) | the API list in **`llms.txt`** *and* `docs/MANUAL.md` §5 |
| A page / route | the page table in **`llms.txt`** *and* the nav in `frontend/src/routes/+layout.svelte` |
| A GHL limit / capability you discovered | `docs/module-capabilities-and-limits.md` |
| A design decision | the relevant `docs/module-specs/NN-*.md` |

**Definition of done = code verifies AND docs match.** Do not mark a task complete, and do not merge into
`dev/Miriam`, with stale docs.

## Backend hygiene (Go)

- **Stdlib only.** No new module in `backend/go.mod` (it has zero `require`s). If you think you need a dependency, stop and ask the lead dev.
- **`go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean before every commit.** Fix vet findings — never commit around them.
- **New-endpoint checklist:** register it in `cmd/server/main.go`; keep ADR-001 (token stays server-side, never in the response); set the GHL version via `store.GHLVersionFor(path)` — never hardcode a `Version` string; put the handler in that module's `handlers/<module>.go`.
- **Decode GHL numbers that can be fractional as `float64`** (e.g. custom-field `position` = `281.25`), not `int`.
- **Errors:** check and return them with a clear HTTP status; never `panic` in a handler; never put a token or secret in an error message or log line.
- **One module per handler file** — match the existing shape; don't pile unrelated logic into one file.
- **No secrets in code, tests, or fixtures** — no `pit-…`, no real location IDs you wouldn't publish.

## Documentation hygiene

- **Markdown lives under `docs/`** (+ root `README.md` + `llms.txt`). Prefer editing an existing doc over adding a new file.
- **Standalone product voice** — no internal-tooling references; this doc set ships with the product.
- **Never paste secrets** — redact tokens as `pit-…`; no live PITs, Neon strings, or keys in any doc.
- **One source of truth:** `MANUAL.md` = user-facing reference; `module-specs/*` = design / decisions; `llms.txt` = the agent map. Update the right one; don't duplicate the same fact in three places.
- **Keep references honest.** If you rename a route / endpoint / file, grep the docs for the old name and fix every hit. Broken links and stale tables are bugs.

## Codex — per-task loop (do this every time)

1. **Read** `llms.txt` + `docs/MANUAL.md` + the module spec for the area you're touching.
2. **Branch:** `git switch dev/Miriam && git pull && git switch -c feature/<slug>`.
3. **Change** the code.
4. **Update the docs** the change affects (see the table above).
5. **Verify:** `go build ./... && go vet ./...` and `npm run check` — both clean.
6. **Commit** code + docs together, with a clear message.
7. **Merge** into `dev/Miriam` (`git switch dev/Miriam && git merge --no-ff feature/<slug>`) → `git push origin dev/Miriam`.
8. **Never** target `main`. That promotion is the lead dev's call.
